# eArchive ↔ eHR: archiving position requests

From the eArchive session, 16/11/2026. For the eHR build session («Έγκριση Θέσεων»), relayed by Marios.
It replaces the reply sent earlier the same day: Marios has now made the four decisions, and the eArchive side is built.
eArchive is ΟΚΥπΥ's protocol and records system (ex-eMetroon; the server paths still say `emetroon`).
This note contains no tokens, secrets or real data.

These go live on the server with the next eArchive deployment (database version 30). Until Marios says the token is in place,
keep items in your outbox. eFinance uses this pattern: write the outbox row in the same transaction as the business event,
send it later, and retry with growing gaps. Never drop an item.

## 1. Where and how

```
POST http://127.0.0.1:5011/api/v1/ingest/documents
Authorization: Bearer <EHR_INGEST_TOKEN>
Idempotency-Key: ehr:<outbox_id>
Content-Type: multipart/form-data
```

- The body has one text part called `meta`, holding JSON (§3), and one binary part per file. Each binary part's
  field name must equal that file's `part_name`.
- **Port 5011** is the eArchive API. 5012 is a static review copy with sample data; it takes nothing.
- **Loopback only.** The route refuses any connection that is not from `127.0.0.1`/`::1`. It also refuses any request
  carrying `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`, `Forwarded`, `CF-Connecting-IP` or `CF-Ray`, even with a valid token.
  Call it directly from the eHR process, never through nginx or Cloudflare.
- **The token** is generated by Marios on the server, in `/opt/emetroon/.env`. He copies it into eHR's settings file
  himself, from file to file, without it being printed. **Tell Marios which file and which setting name eHR reads.**
  It never travels by email or chat.

## 2. Filing

Everything eHR sends is numbered in **ΑΔ** (its own sequence per year) and filed in the site's folder.
The registry comes from the token, so eHR cannot file anywhere else. Site codes for `folder_hints[].hospital`:

| Code | Site | Folder |
|---|---|---|
| `HQ` | Κεντρική Διοίκηση | Φ. ΑΔ.01 |
| `NGH` | Γενικό Νοσοκομείο Λευκωσίας | Φ. ΑΔ.02 |
| `ARC` | Νοσοκομείο Αρχιεπίσκοπος Μακάριος ΙΙΙ | Φ. ΑΔ.03 |
| `LGH` | Γενικό Νοσοκομείο Λεμεσού | Φ. ΑΔ.04 |
| `LAR` | Γενικό Νοσοκομείο Λάρνακας | Φ. ΑΔ.05 |
| `PAP` | Γενικό Νοσοκομείο Πάφου | Φ. ΑΔ.06 |
| `FAM` | Γενικό Νοσοκομείο Αμμοχώστου | Φ. ΑΔ.07 |
| `TRD` | Νοσοκομείο Τροόδους | Φ. ΑΔ.08 |
| `CHR` | Νοσοκομείο Πόλης Χρυσοχούς | Φ. ΑΔ.09 |
| `MH` | Υπηρεσίες Ψυχικής Υγείας | Φ. ΑΔ.10 |
| `HC` | Κέντρα Υγείας | Φ. ΑΔ.11 |
| `CNS` | Κοινοτική Νοσηλευτική | Φ. ΑΔ.12 |

These are eFinance's codes, the same in every ΟΚΥπΥ tool. The old codes `NAM`, `PAF`, `KYP`, `POL`, `MHS` and `PHC` still file in the same folders, as aliases, but send the codes above.

An unknown code gets `400 UNKNOWN_REGISTRY`.

## 3. `meta` fields (schema v1, strict: unknown fields are refused)

**Required:** `schema_version` (1), `outbox_id`, `sent_at` (ISO 8601 with offset), `source_system`,
`source_module`, `source_ref` (≤ 120), `doc_type` (≤ 60), `subject` (3–500), `direction`, `sender_name`,
`letter_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `category`, `classification`, `personal_data`, `folder_hints` (1–5), `files` (1–20).
`personal_data_category` is required when `personal_data` is true.

**Optional:** `sender_ref`, `source_url` (shown, never fetched), `event_date`, `attributes`, `amount` (JSON number,
euros), `currency`, `related`, `approvals`, `counterparties`, `registry_hint`, `retention_class_hint`.

| eHR value | Send it as |
|---|---|
| fixed | `source_system: "eHR"`, `source_module: "position_request"`, `direction: "INTERNAL"`, `category: "Προσλήψεις"` |
| fixed | `personal_data: true`, `personal_data_category: "Στοιχεία προσωπικού"`, `classification: "SENSITIVE"` (`HIGHLY_SENSITIVE` if a request can carry health data or bank details; that also keeps its files away from automatic reading) |
| request number | `source_ref` as in §5, and `sender_ref: "<number>"` |
| date submitted | `letter_date` |
| date decided | `event_date` (leave it out on the submitted deposit) |
| status | `doc_type`, e.g. «Αίτημα θέσης — υποβλήθηκε», «Αίτημα θέσης — εγκρίθηκε», «Αίτημα θέσης — απορρίφθηκε» |
| Directorate | `sender_name`, e.g. «Διεύθυνση Νοσηλευτικών Υπηρεσιών» |
| facility | `folder_hints: [{ "hospital": "NGH" }]` |
| requester and every step | `approvals[]`: `{ actor_name, role, action, at, comment? }`, the requester first with action «Υποβολή»; each one is shown as a decision line on the record |
| employer cost | `amount` + `currency: "EUR"` |
| cost centre, staff category, position title, number of posts | `attributes` (below) |
| subject | the line a clerk would write, e.g. «Αίτημα για 2 θέσεις Νοσηλευτή/τριας, Παθολογική Κλινική» |

**`attributes`** is a flat object of up to 20 values. Keys are lower-case letters, digits and `_` (max 40 characters),
and values are strings up to 300 characters. eArchive shows these four with Greek labels on the record page, and
search finds every value:

```json
"attributes": { "cost_centre": "…", "staff_category": "…", "position_title": "…", "posts": "2" }
```

A key with capitals or spaces gets `400 SCHEMA_INVALID`. Send the number of posts as a string.

## 4. Files

- **One record, many files.** Exactly one `MAIN` (your PDF of the request with its checks and history), and up to 19
  `ATTACHMENT`s (the requester's supporting documents). Each `part_name` must be unique.
- **Limits:** 50 MB per file, 200 MB per deposit.
- **Accepted:** PDF, Word (.doc/.docx), Excel (.xls/.xlsx), PowerPoint, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, GIF, WebP, HTML, plain text,
  CSV, XML, .eml and .msg. A `.zip` is opened and the files inside are stored; each of those must be an accepted type.
  Anything else gets `415 MIME_REJECTED`, which names the file.
- Each `files[]` entry is exactly `{ kind, part_name, filename, mime, size, sha256 }`, all required; `kind` is `MAIN` or `ATTACHMENT`.
- Each file's `size` (bytes) and `sha256` (lowercase hex) must match the bytes, or the deposit gets `400 SHA256_MISMATCH`.
- More than 19 attachments: send them as one `.zip` attachment, which eArchive opens.
- Send UTF-8 filenames in `meta.files[].filename`. That is the name staff see.

## 5. Two deposits per request (decided)

A numbered record is never changed through this route, so every request gives exactly two deposits:

1. **Submitted:** `source_ref: "position_request:<number>:submitted"`.
2. **Decided** (approved, rejected or withdrawn): `source_ref: "position_request:<number>:decided"`, with
   `related: [{ "source_ref": "position_request:<number>:submitted", "relation": "SUPERSEDES" }]`.
   The record page shows the chain. Order doesn't matter: if the decided deposit arrives first, the link is made
   when the submitted one arrives.

Changes between the two are not archived separately; the decided PDF carries the full history.
A request that was decided without ever being sent (an old one, say) sends just the decided deposit.

**Retries cannot file twice:**
- the same `Idempotency-Key` with the same content gets `200` with `Idempotency-Replayed: true` and the original
  receipt; with different content it gets `409 IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH`;
- a second deposit with an already-filed `source_ref` gets `409 DUPLICATE_SOURCE_REF`, and the message names the existing number.

## 6. Who can open them (decided: HR staff only)

ΑΔ is a **closed registry**. Its records, their files, comments and history open only for users whose registry is ΑΔ.
The administrator is not included, and neither is anyone in another registry. Everyone else gets `404`, as if the record did not exist.
Search, lists, the duplicate check and reports leave the records out for them. A link from another record to an ΑΔ record is
hidden from those who cannot open it. Work on an ΑΔ record can be sent only to ΑΔ users, and none can become a circular.
Every opening is recorded in the history log.

Two limits, stated plainly:
- The administrator manages users, and could therefore put someone, themselves included, into ΑΔ. Every such change is in the history log.
- Disposal after 30 years needs the administrator's and the data protection officer's approval. On the retention screen
  they see the register line (number, subject, dates), not the record or its files. Keep names out of `subject`.

## 7. Retention (decided: 30 years)

Class `rc-hr`, for every outcome: kept to 31 December of the year of filing plus 30. Then the record becomes a disposal candidate.
Two different people approve, and the files are destroyed 30 days later. The register line stays, marked as disposed.
A legal hold stops all of this.

**Notices back to eHR:** when an eHR record is disposed of, or a legal hold is set or cleared, eArchive can call eHR at
an address on `127.0.0.1`. It sends `{ event, protocol_id, protocol_number, source_ref, at }` with the same bearer token,
and retries with growing gaps until it gets a 2xx. The events are `protocol.deleted`, `legal_hold.set` and `legal_hold.cleared`.
Answer 200 to event types you don't know, otherwise later notices wait behind the one you refused. This is switched off until
eHR gives an address (setting `EHR_EVENTS_URL` on our side).

## 8. Answers

| Answer | Meaning | eHR should |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | filed: `{ protocol_id, protocol_number, url, registry, received_at }` | store `protocol_id` and `protocol_number` on the request; show the number, with `url` as the link; mark sent |
| `200` + `Idempotency-Replayed: true` | already filed | treat as `201` |
| connection refused, timeout, `5xx` | eArchive down or restarting (a few seconds) | retry with backoff, same key: safe |
| `409 IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH` | same key, different content | bug on your side: stop and alert |
| `409 DUPLICATE_SOURCE_REF` | already filed | do not retry; record the number from the message |
| `400 SCHEMA_INVALID` / `SHA256_MISMATCH` / `UNKNOWN_REGISTRY` | the deposit is wrong | do not retry unchanged; alert |
| `401`, `403 LOOPBACK_ONLY` / `SERVICE_ONLY` / `SOURCE_MISMATCH` | token or network wrong | alert; retrying won't help |
| `413`, `415 MIME_REJECTED`, `400 ARCHIVE_*` | too big / type not allowed / bad zip | show the reason; do not retry unchanged |

eArchive files one deposit at a time, so a burst waits rather than failing; use a 60-second timeout.
Error bodies are `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details"? } }`. On `409 DUPLICATE_SOURCE_REF`, `error.details` holds `{ protocol_id, protocol_number }`.
A retry must resend identical `meta` (including `sent_at`): any changed value is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH`.
The `url` works for staff once the eArchive web app is published with sign-in (IT pending). Until then, show the number.

## 9. What we need from eHR

1. The settings file and setting name where eHR reads the token, so Marios can copy it in.
2. An address for the notices in §7, if eHR wants them.
3. Two or three sample deposits with made-up data: one submitted, one approved with attachments, one rejected.
   eArchive runs them through its own test before the first real one is sent.
